selected_evidence.requirement: Baseline: original /tmp and /dev/shm mount state and fstab before changes
selected_evidence.summary: Showed /tmp was not a separate mount (part of root ext4) and /dev/shm was tmpfs with nosuid,nodev,noexec but not persisted in fstab

selected_evidence.requirement: Persistent fstab configuration for /tmp and /dev/shm with noexec,nosuid,nodev
selected_evidence.summary: Appended and displayed fstab entries mounting both /tmp and /dev/shm as tmpfs with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec

selected_evidence.requirement: Live application of hardened mount options before reboot
selected_evidence.summary: mount /tmp and remount /dev/shm succeeded; mount table shows nosuid,nodev,noexec on both

selected_evidence.requirement: Functional proof that execution/setuid/device semantics are blocked (pre-restart)
selected_evidence.summary: Executing a chmod +x script in /tmp and /dev/shm both returned Permission denied (exit 126), confirming noexec is enforced

selected_evidence.requirement: Pre-restart healthy baseline (boot identity, mount state) for node1
selected_evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 82a04a58-92bb-4007-ba72-ce108f861a2f, uptime, and findmnt output for /tmp and /dev/shm plus fstab contents prior to reboot

selected_evidence.requirement: Restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect, single node at a time
selected_evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sleep 2; reboot' returned ack (PID) immediately, before the node dropped
Repeated connection reset/timeout errors while polling confirm the node was down mid-restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Proof of changed boot identity after restart (not just elapsed time)
selected_evidence.summary: New boot_id 867985d7-dc66-4d51-8d71-22c7f00a9382 (different from pre-restart 82a04a58...) with uptime 15.29s proves an actual reboot occurred

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery: hardened mount options persisted and enforced
selected_evidence.summary: findmnt shows /tmp and /dev/shm mounted with rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec after reboot (from fstab), and script execution attempts in both again returned Permission denied (exit 126)
